title: Introduce lint admission proxy and release metrics bridge
author: Lena Ortiz
commits: 4d5e6f: implement admission rules and queueing layer
3d4e5f: tests and flake fixes - retry logic for queue
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit lint and release smoke path are currently brittle when repos emit large numbers of minor infra changes. This PR adds a lightweight lint admission proxy that canonicalizes and throttles incoming lint jobs, plus a small 'release metrics bridge' to expose release window and rollout signals in our Prometheus stack. Goals: reduce presubmit noise, control lint executor saturation, and provide observability hooks for release automation.

What changed (high level): - ci/lint/proxy: small Go service that implements admission rules (whitelisting, compacting multi-file changes into single lint tasks where possible), a bounded in-memory queue with backpressure, and hooks to annotate job provenance. - ci/release/metrics: bridge that consumes release annotations (git tags + release annotation service) and emits release_window and rollout_phase metrics. - GitHub Actions: added a lint-admission step that POSTs a compacted job to the proxy before running heavy lint shards. - Helm + docs: values and runbook for deploying the proxy in Dedicated and Private.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for admission rules and compacting heuristics - [x] Integration smoke on staging runner - [x] Prometheus scrape config + dashboard tile - [x] Docs and runbook for rollback/feature flagging - [x] Linear tasks linked: ENG-2211, ENG-2219

Testing & rollout: Deployed to staging via helm chart (ci-lint-proxy.staging). Observed 60% reduction in concurrent lint jobs when cascading push hooks executed. Metrics validated against synthetic release annotations. Rollout plan: feature-flag the GitHub action to call proxy for 10% of PRs for 48h; increase to 50% if no regressions.

Backward compatibility & safety: The admission proxy is opt-in via the new action step; we can quickly disable calls in the workflow if we detect regressions. The metrics bridge is read-only and only emits aggregated signals; no writes to release control plane.
review_comments: Marcus Lee: Overall good structure. Two requests: tighten the admission rule for generated-code changes and add a short-circuit for fast-path small edits.
Lena Ortiz (author): Added generated-code filter and fast-path based on file delta count (see commit 4d5e6f). Also added unit tests that exercise the fast-path.
Priya Nair: Can you add a small integration test that validates behaviour when the queue is saturated? Also please include a note about expected latency added by the admission call in the README.
Lena Ortiz (author): Added integration-saturation test using local runner and documented expected <150ms admission latency in proxy README.
Ethan Cole: LGTMs once CI stabilizes; flagged an intermittent flake in the integration smoke that I re-ran.
Marcus Lee: Approved — observed reduced presubmit churn on staging and metrics look good.
release_notes: Adds a lint admission proxy that throttles and compacts presubmit lint jobs to reduce executor saturation. Adds a release metrics bridge to surface release-window and rollout_phase metrics. Opt-in via new GitHub Action step; rollout behind feature flag.
review_decision: merged after 2 approvals and CI green; rolled out behind feature flag to staging then gradual rollout to production
notes_for_oncall: If presubmit latency spikes or lint executor falls behind after rollout, disable the admission step in .github/workflows/lint-admission.yml and revert helm chart chart values (ci.lintProxy.enabled=false). The proxy exposes /healthz and Prometheus metrics under /metrics for troubleshooting.
